proposed_status_reason: Supervisor decision requested: A for all scalar input domains and the serialized ordinary-RAM L1/bridge projection. Original matched C is also checked symbolically after explicit width adaptation. L0 machine linkage remains C, with D reaching only byte swap; do not promote the whole chain to A or claim D reaches the two unused public entries.

original.provenance: The original functions remain in src/c/module.c, Borland C++ 3.0 -mh -2. Fresh isolated cjudge.compare verifies all 23 functions (7074 bytes) and ordered TU relocations against the locked expanded oracle. This is a C contribution proof, not a new full packed-file proof.

native.bridge: All three canonical L1 endpoints replaced together, with no L1 fallback. Original definitions remain renamed l1_* in generated copies under this worker's build directory. No shared audio state type introduced.

purpose: Reverse a container size's byte order, disable recurring main-track section restoration while the C playing word is nonzero, and report elapsed ADLX timing units using unsigned wrapped clock difference. No playback, scanning, timer or device ownership is transferred.

inputs: Disable: arbitrary uint16_t playing and enabled words; returns the next enabled word.
Elapsed: arbitrary uint32_t ticks and origin, arbitrary uint16_t rate. No device, playing, loaded-track or positive-clock invariant.
outputs: Byte swap: uint32_t with reversed bytes.
Disable: zero iff playing is nonzero, otherwise original enabled word. Bridge always returns AX=1.

Elapsed: MUSIC_CLOCK_OK plus ((ticks-origin) modulo 2^32)/rate when rate!=0. MUSIC_CLOCK_DIVIDE_BY_ZERO with no meaningful units when rate==0. Bridge returns UGH_UNSUPPORTED on fault and leaves AX/DX unchanged; this represents the L0 fault rather than simulating fault-handler execution.
effects: Ordinary native functions have no persistent storage, allocation, devices or indirect calls.
Disable bridge reads only the playing word; only while nonzero does it write the two loop-enable bytes to zero. It does not read the old enable word or write on the inactive path.
Elapsed bridge reads the two dwords and rate, writes no RAM; byte swap bridge reads four argument bytes and writes no RAM.
Bridge retains SOUND ES output for disable and elapsed, AX/DX value convention, all other L1 registers/flags, and the untouched input argument/return frame.
preconditions: Serialized operation over ordinary RAM; no instruction-level IRQ delivery inside an operation.
Bridge cdecl arguments and return/save scratch do not overlap SOUND storage, devices or live code. Symbolic shell proof uses disjoint canonical SS:SP; arbitrary register values otherwise.
Original Borland unsigned long is 32 bits and unsigned/int are 16 bits; little-endian byte-object representation for the original swap C proof. Native swap itself is host-endian independent.
Arithmetic flags and compiler-volatile scratch beyond the existing L1 ABI are not semantic C results. Arbitrary external machine-code callers depending on them are outside this closure contract.

SwapDwordByteOrder: C:LoadAdlibTrackData, calls at 0878:0B5A, 0BA9, 0C57. Each PUSH CS/near CALL is a far cdecl frame. ADD SP,4 immediately follows each call, replacing arithmetic flags; only AX of the result is consumed. DX is redefined before use. All 32 output bits are retained anyway.

First two calls reverse BE32 AHDR/IMAP sizes then use low 16 bits to advance a far offset. Third reverses BE32 ADLX root size, subtracts 34 and stores low 16-bit event extent. TRCK's duplicate LE32 length is not consumed by these functions.

memory.record_12_analysis: AudioChannelStates base 0014, stride 002A: slot 12 occupies 020C..0235 inclusive. Its +06 start pointer=0212, +0A stream length=0216, +10 cursor=021C, +1E deadline=022A/022C, +22 voice count=022E, +28 flags=0234. All five projected fields are OUTSIDE that record. Guard at 0236 separates it from rate/clock/origin. These functions do not read/write a descriptor, instrument map, scan cursor, voice array, bank pointer, fade state or timer period. Any future record-12 view must alias these main descriptor fields once, not duplicate them alongside SOUND globals. No blanket 42-byte sample struct should absorb the clock fields.
memory.proposed_typed_view_analysis_only: A borrowed music-clock/control view with raw uint16_t playing, section_loop_enabled, ticks_per_unit and uint32_t ticks, time_origin. Map high-word names onto the two dwords; give all five one common audio storage owner. Pass snapshots as scalar inputs to this unit; publish only the conditional enable-word write. Keep this proposed view distinct from the main-track descriptor overlay, fade clock and PIT period. This is analysis only; no shared native audio types are introduced.
memory.alias_and_order_limits: The five spans do not overlap each other. SOUND bulk clears alias them, and unchecked malformed record indices could reach adjacent globals; these services impose no false independence invariant on their values. L0 elapsed reads rate first, tick HIGH then LOW, origin LOW then HIGH, without CLI. L1/bridge read ticks, origin, rate. Arbitrary observed scalar values (including torn values) are admitted, but equivalence for identical mid-instruction IRQ schedules is not asserted. Stable serialized snapshots commute; no stronger coherence protocol is inferred.

assumptions: No positivity or reachability restriction on elapsed clock/origin/rate, nor canonical boolean restriction on playing/loop words.
The original C byte-swap object accesses use a 4-byte little-endian uint32_t in the harness, adapting only the historical unsigned-long width and function names.
No live-stack alias or device-backed SOUND storage; existing routine observation excludes transient save scratch below entry frame.
No instruction-level asynchronous IRQ proof. There are no internal callbacks, service points, event acknowledgements or synchronization operations in this unit.
